elements.element: Customer may assign without Vendor consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "The Company may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: "HDI may not assign without the Company's prior written consent"

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment not to be unreasonably withheld
Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "and never to a competitor of the Company"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: Condition demonstrably absent: neither the original Section 10.3 nor the insertion creates any change-of-control termination or deemed-assignment right for HDI; deterministic check confirms "preferred assignment adds no change-of-control deemed-assignment rule".

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: HDI's assignment is conditioned on consent: "HDI may not assign without the Company's prior written consent" — no reciprocal successor right
No notice mechanic appears; insertion says only "without consent to an affiliate or to a successor"

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld

reasons: The single inserted sentence completes every atomic element of the preferred position: Customer affiliate and M&A successor assignment without consent, Vendor assignment only with Customer's consent not unreasonably withheld, and an absolute bar on assignment to a Customer competitor.
The no-Vendor-termination-on-change-of-control element is satisfied by absence: the clause creates no change-of-control termination or deemed-assignment right, so nothing needed to be struck.
Fallback is not independently satisfied (no mutual successor-assignment right and no written-notice mechanic), but the locked target is preferred and the levels are not mixed.

Minimality holds: one concise sentence added to a clause that previously said nothing about assignment; the original successors-and-assigns sentence is left untouched and no new definitions, exceptions, or dangling mechanics are introduced.
